dialog.body: Finance department, this is Luis. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, I think I'm in the right place. I got a parking ticket thing in the mail, sort of, but it's not really from you guys directly. It came through a rental car company.
Okay. Those happen. The rental company pays it, then passes it along to whoever had the car. Do you have the ticket number handy?

I think so, hold on. Maybe it's on the second page. Okay, so there's a letter from the rental company, and then behind it there's the, um, the citation. The number is... I think it's four, four, one, seven, nine, zero, two.
Four four one seven nine zero two. Let me pull that up. Bear with me, my computer's got one speed and it's called thoughtful.
Ha, okay. Take your time. I've got nowhere to be, I guess.
Alright, I've got it. Overtime meter violation on Thames Street, back in October. Is that right?

Yeah, I think that's it. I was in town for a weekend, I was maybe ten minutes over, if that. And now the rental company is, sort of, charging me this whole administrative fee on top. It's way more than the ticket. I think it's like triple.
Yeah, that part's the rental company's doing. They tack on a handling fee. The city's portion is just the fine itself. That's the only part I can see or touch.
Right, right. So, I think I already paid the city part. Maybe. I sent something in October, I believe, when I got the first notice. So why is it coming again?

Let me look at the payment history. Hmm. I do see a payment posted on the twenty-first of October. Then the rental company's payment shows up later, which may be the overlap. Do you know what card you used?
I think it was my Visa, maybe. The last four are, um, sort of, three, three, five, eight. Three three five eight.
Three three five eight. That matches the payment I'm looking at. So you paid, and then the rental company paid too, because the notice went to them first.
So I paid twice. Basically. I think that's what you're telling me.
Basically, the city got paid twice on that ticket. Which sounds like a refund situation, but I can't promise how it'll go until it's reviewed. I can flag it for a duplicate payment review.
Okay, yeah, please do that. That's, I mean, that's kind of annoying. I did the right thing and now I'm chasing it.
Understood. I'll note the date of your payment and the card ending in three three five eight, so they don't have to ask you again.
Okay. Um, can I also get the photo? Of the violation. I think there was a photo, maybe. The letter said there's one. I'd like to see it, because I'm not sure the car was even where they say.
There is an image attached to the record. I can email it to you. What email address do you want it sent to?

Oh, sure. Hold on, my friend gave me a list of questions to ask, sort of a cheat sheet. I think the email one is on there. Anyway, it's rocco dot conti, all one word after the dot, at a mail dot com. Maybe I should spell it. R-O-C-C-O, dot, C-O-N-T-I.
Got it. Rocco dot Conti at a mail dot com. I'll send the photo over this afternoon. Should land within the hour, unless the computer decides otherwise.
Okay. And what else is on this list. Um. He wrote down to ask for a confirmation of the review. Like something in writing, I think.
Your friend's thorough. I'll put a note on the account, and the review outcome gets mailed out. What's the mailing address on file? I have one Carroll Avenue listed.
Yeah, that's me. One sixty-nine Carroll Avenue, in the Fifth Ward. That's right.
Perfect, one sixty-nine Carroll. And a callback number in case they have questions?
Sure, it's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-seven.
Four oh one, five five five, oh one eight seven. Got it. Anything else I can do for you today?
I think that's it. I mean, there's one more thing on the list, but it's, like, about parking permits, and it's not really what I called about. So no.
Fair enough. Watch your email for the photo, and the duplicate review will come by mail.
Okay. Thanks. I guess I'll wait and see.
You do that. Have a good afternoon, Mr. Conti.
Yeah, you too.
